Rishi / team — reviewed the binder and the requests. Quick summary and follow-ups:

1) Occurrence vs Claim-made: InsureCo currently issues CGL on a claim-made basis for Acme's account. Converting to occurrence is a material change and typically not available mid-policy without a re-underwrite; it would be a new policy and likely requires a new quote and underwriting, which will delay.
2) Retroactive date & ERP: We can confirm a retroactive date back to 2019 for the current policy period, so that looks fine. ERP (tail) can be purchased; rough estimate for a 3-year ERP is 12-18% of the annual premium — final pricing after submission.
3) Additional Insured & WoS endorsements: We can issue CG 20 10/11 or equivalent depending on the carrier. However, note the standard Additional Insured endorsement excludes Professional Services for certain acts, and that can be negotiated but may require higher premium or specific language. WoS endorsement can be added for covered operations.
4) Professional Liability gap: Our CGL may exclude some professional exposures (e.g., negligent design of ML models). If Acme requires coverage for professional services, they likely need Technology/Errors & Omissions cover (separate policy). We can provide a combined package quote.

Action items for Redwood/Acme to confirm: 
- Confirm whether Acme will accept claim-made with the retroactive date + ERP instead of occurrence.
- Provide the exact Additional Insured wording you plan to include (we can mark up to show where carrier may carve back).
- Confirm whether professional services performed by Redwood should be covered under Acme's CGL or Redwood's own E&O — Contracts should decide which party carries that risk.

I’ll prepare a formal binder quote and sample endorsements once you confirm the above.

Regards,
